jobs.text: IOM, UN Migration Agency in Beirut, Lebanon is looking for a Programme Officer (Infrastructure) who will be responsible and accountable for the technical coordination, management and oversight of assigned infrastructure projects within IOM Lebanon’s IBG portfolio. 23854 Programme Officer (Infrastructure) (P) Professional 2026-11-06T06:39:58+00:00 2026-11-19T22:59:00+00:00 Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates: Internal candidates Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: Bahamas, Barbados, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu Second tier candidates include: All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM. Organizational Context and Scope The International Organization for Migration (IOM) office in Lebanon is responding to changing border management needs in a complex operational and humanitarian setting, particularly at land borders. Mixed migration flows and increased mobility influenced by regional dynamics highlight the need for enhanced operational capacity to ensure safe, orderly, and effective border operations. In this context, IOM Lebanon supports national border management authorities to strengthen border infrastructure and operational readiness. This includes interventions supporting the rehabilitation, upgrade or full reconstruction of key border crossing points across the country. Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programmes, under the direct supervision of the Immigration and Border Governance (IBG) Programme Manager, and in coordination with relevant Programme Managers (PMs), the Regional Office (RO) for the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and relevant units at Headquarters (HQ), the Programme Officer (Infrastructure) will be responsible and accountable for the technical coordination, management, and oversight of assigned infrastructure projects within IOM Lebanon’s IBG portfolio. IOM, UN Migration Agency in Beirut, Lebanon is looking for a Programme Officer (Infrastructure) who will be responsible and accountable for the technical coordination, management and oversight of assigned infrastructure projects within IOM Lebanon’s IBG portfolio. en Beirut, Lebanon LB 6 Required Qualifications and Experience Education Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Project Management, or Construction Management, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or, University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Progressive professional experience in the management and supervision of large-scale international civil engineering and infrastructure development projects; Demonstrated experience in the design, rehabilitation, and construction of public infrastructure and institutional facilities, including preparation and review of technical documentation such as drawings, BOQs, technical specifications, and cost estimates; Experience in contract management of construction works, including preparation of technical specifications, bid evaluation, and contract administration; Experience working with governmental authorities, UN agencies, donors, and other stakeholders in a multi-partner environment, including familiarity with UN and bilateral donor programming, reporting requirements, and compliance standards; Experience in border infrastructure projects, including the design, construction, and rehabilitation of border crossing points, is a strong advantage; and, Experience working in the Middle East and North Africa regions is an advantage. The position is located within the Immunization Supplies cone, in the EPI Unit. Within the Immunization Supplies cone, the EPI Unit is accountable for supply, procurement, and market shaping for the portfolio of vaccines that include HepB, BCG, Diphtheria containing vaccines (Td, DTP and DT), Penta, Hexa, Hib and Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines for routine, outbreak immunization activities; and engaging in technical partnerships to facilitate access to novel TB vaccines. Purpose for the job: Under the general guidance of the Senior Contracts Manager, Vaccine Centre, the incumbent is responsible for the planning, development and implementation of procurement of a range of vaccines working with vaccine programme partners, overseeing market research and long-range procurement planning in order to achieve the most appropriate and cost-effective means of procurement. This job profile will be supervising the relevant staff required to perform the activities as defined within the Contract Specialist Terms of Reference. Key functions, accountabilities and related duties/tasks: Procurement: Support timely development of procurement strategies, oversee procurement of vaccine materials. Oversee supplier relationships and contracts management to ensure supplier compliance with LTA’s and purchase order terms and conditions. Ensure all procurement activities are in compliance with the UNICEF Financial Rules and Regulations, Supply Procedures and Guidance Notes, and all other applicable procurement procedures. Oversee and advise requisitioning Country Office/Regional Office regarding contractual conditions and supplier appraisals for purchasing of products. Undertake manufacturer missions to troubleshoot and ensure supplier management and oversight, as required. Create awareness and understanding of the need for adequate quality standards, best practice and do-no-harm policies. Ensure policy guidelines and regulatory requirements are appropriate and consistently applied to UNICEF procurement in close collaboration with the team of multidisciplinary technical specialists and officers. Ensure compliance with Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP), ISO and other relevant international regulations, standards and guidelines, including integration of Quality Management Systems (QMS) requirements into work processes and functions. Partnerships: Engage with relevant market shaping partners such as [Gavi Alliance, WHO, Gates Foundation] Oversee engagement with disease programme teams and extended partners to provide the supply and demand perspectives to guide global programme decisions. Contribute to UNICEF led or other industry consultations and immunization meetings. Represent UNICEF Supply Division at partner meetings pertaining to immunization to represent supply perspective. Supervision: Establish work plans and priorities, monitor achievements, and evaluate performance of support staff. Ensure timely reporting and communication of critical information in support of transparency. Contribute to capacity building and knowledge sharing within the team and throughout the Centre. Perform other duties or assignments as requested by the supervisor. The recent flooding in Rasuwa and downstream districts along the Bhotekoshi corridor caused significant damage to schools and education infrastructure, disrupting learning for thousands of children. Rapid assessments identified extensive damage to classrooms, learning spaces, WASH facilities, and educational equipment, requiring immediate support to restore access to education. UNICEF, in collaboration with government counterparts and Education Cluster partners, is supporting the continuation of learning through temporary learning arrangements, provision of learning materials, psychosocial support, and early recovery interventions. As the response progresses from emergency relief to recovery, there is a growing need for technical oversight to ensure that temporary and semi-permanent learning facilities are designed, constructed, and monitored in line with safety, quality, and child-friendly standards. Nepal is highly vulnerable to climate-induced disasters and earthquakes, which frequently damage education infrastructure and disrupt children's learning. Timely technical support is critical to assess damage, identify appropriate learning-space solutions, adapt designs to local contexts, and provide guidance to partners and communities during the establishment of temporary and transitional learning facilities. Furthermore, the Government of Nepal has recently endorsed the Comprehensive School Safety Master Plan, reinforcing its commitment to ensuring that schools are safe, resilient, and prepared for future hazards. The recovery phase presents an important opportunity to operationalize and advance the principles of the Master Plan by integrating risk-informed and resilient approaches into the design, rehabilitation, and reconstruction of education facilities. Technical engineering support is therefore essential not only to restore learning spaces but also to ensure that recovery investments contribute to safer and more resilient schools. To address these needs, UNICEF seeks to maintain standby engineering support through an Education in Emergencies Engineer. The consultant will provide technical guidance for the assessment, planning, design, construction, and monitoring of temporary and semi-permanent learning facilities; support government and partner-led recovery interventions; promote the integration of Comprehensive School Safety principles into education infrastructure activities; and ensure that all interventions meet agreed technical standards, are safe for children, and facilitate the rapid resumption and continuity of learning during emergencies and recovery efforts. jobs.text: UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence. UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to a Champion Ethiopia is situated in the Horn of Africa and is the second most populous country on the continent, with an estimated population of 115 million. It borders six African countries: Djibouti, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan, and covers 1,104,300 square kilometers. Approximately 85 percent of the population lives in rural areas. Ethiopia represents a melting pot of ancient cultures, with Middle Eastern and African cultures evident in the religious, ethnic, and language composition of its people.
